human_tolerance.notes: Very common and popular garden bird; visits bird tables and feeders, readily accepts nest boxes, and is abundant in urban parks and gardens even in noise-polluted areas.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Territories are established and defended from late January; in Europe egg-laying usually begins after March, clutch typically 5-12 (up to 18 recorded); second broods common.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: In autumn and winter, great tits join mixed-species foraging flocks with other tits and finches; irruptive movements of up to a thousand birds occur in harsh winters.

vocalizations.description: Up to 40 types of calls and songs; the male's familiar territorial song is a loud, repeated two-note 'teacher, teacher', likened to a squeaky wheelbarrow wheel, given mainly from late winter into summer.
A loud 'tink' contact/alarm note used by adult males in territorial disputes and when disturbed; soft 'pit', 'spick' or 'chit' notes are used as ordinary contact calls.

range.note: Country list derived from the Distribution section and the subspecies list: all of Europe except Iceland and northern Scandinavia (including Balearic, Corsican, Sardinian, Cretan, Cypriot and Aegean island populations), Morocco/Algeria/Tunisia in North Africa, the Middle East (Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Jordan, Iran, Azerbaijan), Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Afghanistan) and northern Asia from the Urals to northern China, Mongolia and the Amur Valley.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Forages by foliage-gleaning and hopping through branches and on the ground; flies between perches, like other Paridae.

traits.nest_type.note: Cavity nester, usually in a tree hole, occasionally a wall or rock face; readily takes to nest boxes.

traits.mass_kg.note: Averaged from two sourced values: Wikidata (P2067) 18.5 g and EltonTraits BirdFuncDat (Dunning 2008) 16.25 g.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No explicit life-expectancy figure was found in the English Wikipedia article, Wikidata or ITIS for Parus major. Inferred, as a close-relative estimate, from the same value already sourced (via BTO ring-recovery survival statistics) for the congeneric, similarly sized blue tit (Cyanistes caeruleus) in this repository; both are small, high-first-year-mortality cavity-nesting Paridae with comparable life history. A reviewer should look for a better direct source if one becomes available.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits BirdFuncDat: Diet-Inv 40, Diet-Scav 10, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Nect 10, Diet-Seed 20 (mapped to schema categories invertebrate/carrion/fruit/nectar/seed). Wikipedia confirms a primarily insectivorous diet in summer, with berries, seeds (beech, hazel) and bird-table scraps added in autumn and winter; Diet-Scav is interpreted as scavenged human food (table scraps, feeders), not dead-animal carrion.

traits.social.note: Socially monogamous breeding pairs defend territories (though extra-pair copulation is frequent); joins mixed-species flocks in autumn/winter, captured separately as the 'flocking' seasonal phase.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Diurnal forager; no nocturnal activity described other than the 2009 record of killing roosting (hibernating) pipistrelle bats in winter, which is not routine foraging behaviour.

traits.defense.note: Modelled as the shared behaviour program's alarm-then-flee-to-perch response; Wikipedia documents the Eurasian sparrowhawk as a predator and a loud 'tink' alarm/territorial call, which the shared program represents.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a very common, popular garden bird that readily visits feeders, bird tables and nest boxes and is abundant even in noisy urban areas; set comparable to other tame garden Paridae.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat gives ground 0, understory 20, midhigh 60, canopy 20 (all arboreal strata). However, Wikipedia explicitly states great tits 'often forage on the ground, particularly in years with high beech mast production', a stronger ground-foraging claim than for the congeneric blue tit, so ground share was set higher than EltonTraits alone would give; judgement blend of the two sources.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Cavity nester and roosts in tree holes/cavities, occasionally walls or rock faces; matches the 'cavity' resource tag directly.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrates mainly in the breeding season; seeds (beech, hazel) and fruit/berries in autumn and winter (Wikipedia); scavenged food (bird-table scraps, feeders, suet) especially in severe winters ('may consume 44% of their body weight in sunflower seeds'); nectar resource reflects EltonTraits' Diet-Nect share, given no direct great-tit source describes nectar/bud feeding, so months and weight are a judgement carried over from the diet split; nest and roost sites from Wikipedia.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Garden, feeder and nest-box use, and abundance in noise-polluted urban areas (with a documented song-frequency shift), from Wikipedia; light_max authored (judgement).

seasonal.strategy.note: 'The great tit is generally not migratory. Pairs will usually remain near or in their territory year round.'

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window: territories established/defended from late January, egg-laying usually begins after March in Europe, most breeding between January and September; end-of-season and flocking window are judgement based on the described winter mixed-species flocking and irruptive movements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Nestling period 16-22 days, independent 8 days after fledging, with extended parental feeding up to 25 (first brood) or 50 days (second brood); duration_days (90) and scale are a rough judgement estimate to the first moult, following the same approach used for the congeneric blue tit.

vocalizations.song.note: Territorial 'teacher, teacher' song and general timing from the Voice section; season_months, loudness and cooldown are judgement.

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'Tink' alarm/territorial-dispute call and soft contact notes from the Voice section; loudness and cooldown are judgement.

look.note: Bluish-black crown, black neck/throat/bib/head, white cheeks and ear coverts, broad black ventral mid-line stripe, olive-green back tinged olive, bluish-grey wings with white wing-bar, bluish-grey tail with white outer tips; proportions authored (judgement).

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program (judgement).
